steps.name: Logos
steps.text: So this time it's Iberia.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Patience, Banshee. These were the most unforgettable days for me.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I thought you wouldn't like it there.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: I certainly didn't like Iberia before that disaster. All that self-aggrandizing, all so self-obsessed. I was through with it.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: They didn't understand fear.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Whereupon that disaster satisfied you?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: I'm not some twisted psychopath like Old Red-Eye is. The disaster itself was nothing unordinary. When has the land ever been short of disaster?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: But those creatures fascinated me.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I've only heard rumors. If I'll be honest, those things duly disturb me.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: They are too removed from us.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Then how removed do you consider me from you, Banshee?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: You should know, no matter what aspect I take, none of it is the real me.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Originium leaves an irrefutable brand upon all. It has you walk in the forms you do upon this terra firma.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: But the one thing it forgot was the Damazti.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Only we still preserve our firstborn form.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Are you proud of your purity?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: No, no. With this world in the state it is, what does purity even mean anymore?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: I can only chase after the changes it brings. I can only chase after you. Chase all you create.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Every manner of means possible I used. I found in Iberia a wasted town. I moved in there.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: We moved in there.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: We made that town run anew. Work, communication, trade, traffic...

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Two hundred mes made up one small town.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I can't say whether you're lucky or unlucky not to have fallen into insanity yet.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Hah. Who knows.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: In any case, the time I spent there left a deep impression on me. With so much to manage, I was drowning every day in it.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: It gave me the false sense... that we lived meaningfully.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: But weariness came in the end, as it always does. Giving my undivided attention to the trivial was very amusing, but even summed all together, it still could not give me the answer I was seeking.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Until I found them. I heard some call the things 'Seaborn.'

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: I observed them for a very long time.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: They reminded you of yourself.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: No. In terms of unity, we far surpass the Seaborn and their many.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: No matter how many appearances we divide into, we are in the end a whole, while the Seaborn have only the choice of joining with the many.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: But, you know what? I envy them.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: They need nothing more than to heed their instincts.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Find food, find nutrients, multiply, evolve.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Perhaps that word you slung just now, 'purity,' should be falling on them.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: While I... I remain where I was, watching it all, watching those variegated little beings assimilate a swathe of seagrass with them.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: They think nothing. They do what they're meant to do.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: And what of us? What are our instincts? And what are we meant to do?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Banshee, can you give us any suggestions?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Are you laughing?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Apologies, Damazti. I am not mocking you, by far.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: They who could proclaim themselves the oldest King of the Royal Court, Their Majesties the Damazti, are simply looking for the meaning of their life.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: It's a very important thing, of course it is. I just never would've thought, that standing before me... was a wayward philosopher.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: Would you ever guess the years I've spent a professor of philosophy at Victoria's universities?

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: To you, seeking meaning is easy. Excluding the least minority of existences, life can always be considered brief.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: You find a goal for yourself, to stuff the days full with so that it isn't so tough.

steps.name: 'Iberian'
steps.text: But we cannot do that.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: From your suggestions to Theresis's future, none of it holds our interest.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: To us, it is no more than passing the time.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Why do we hold affection for these things that pass in the blink of an eye?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We've exhausted practically every possibility, and practically every delight too.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I'm beginning to pity you, Damazti.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: You've found out we're just some old decrepit nothing gets to anymore, no matter how loud you shout it.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Not many know this secret.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: A few friends of mine taught me this silly game...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: No, never mind.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Go on, Banshee. We're more interested than you suppose.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: But—you may have to wait a moment. Some bothersome work has come a-knocking.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Not here, that is, but I'm afraid we'll need to divert a little attention.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What do you mean... not there?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I mean it's not there, for god's sakes!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The comms post isn't there! There's nothing there! Someone's made off with it!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Was it the Dublinn forces?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Afraid it was long before that. Judging from how thick the dust was, someone must've been eyeing it when Norport was just setting course away from Londinium.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The Redsteel Guard captain would never genuinely be fooled by us. He'd be very quick to realize the projected message was never sent.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But at the very least, we're back at the same starting line. We have a renewed opportunity to go for the gold.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: First there was you for the Duke of Caster, now there's Dublinn's spectre force...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You've all secretly infiltrated to get onto this plate, which means, you want to keep up Norport's surface appearances.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Without any way to force the dukes' main armies into mobilizing, our plan's dead in the water.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Never try that excuse again, Delphine.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: As long as your duke mother learns you're still here, she'll find some way to save you, won't she.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I can't guarantee...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Admitting you get along with your mother is nothing to be ashamed of.

options: Do you have an idea, Ines?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: What a pain in the ass.

options: Looks like you can do it.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: ...I really hate that part of you.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But alright. I can try.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I need high elevation. Don't get your hopes up.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Miss Ines, how much time will your idea need?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Until sunup.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Tell Siege and her city friends to get ready.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: May I wish you all godspeed, and I look forward to you choosing the Sunset Street Hotel again.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I've spent some wonderful times here, and gotten to know some very fine people.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Norport is a lovely, thriving place. Don't let it be reduced to memories and rubble like this.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We promise, sir.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There'll come an end to the conspiracy and dispute.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There's... a person I truly, truly miss, who once told me...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That perhaps, one day... everyone on this vast land can fall into peaceful slumber.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: *sigh* There's a back-breaker. This hotel's even messier than it was before.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: People who don't do their own cleaning never know how difficult it is to maintain a bit of order.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Percival! Percival!

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Where's she run off to now...

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Fine, go and leave this old codger by himself for a bit.
The age-riddled hotel owner finds an equally age-riddled armchair, and opts to find a comfortable position before sitting down.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: So that... Cautus girl, she's the King of Sarkaz?

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: It's getting harder and harder to keep up with all this change. Even I'm a little shocked by it.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Change... change. Maybe I've been slacking on that sort of change myself.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Change isn't progress, after all.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Alright, about time I bid farewell to this old friend. To tell the truth... I really did love this place.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: *sigh*... Two more months you should've kept this up, Colbert. Who would've imagined, after two months of the Sarkaz army in the city, an old devil would go from cleaner to hotel owner.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: I just can't wrap my head around it.
The elderly Sarkaz stands up, and scans over the grand lobby of the public house. Every single article in here is near and dear to him.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: That Ines Caprinae says war doesn't do metaphor.

steps.name: Colbert
steps.text: Well, then. Let's restore its original looks.
Upon a finely woven rug that's seen more political players and aristocrats than anyone could know, the elderly Sarkaz drops a lighter lit aflame.
And swiftly, the fires rage high.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: The... The soldiers here, were they all killed?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Is the enemy here?! If I'd found this earlier...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Their families will receive compensation payouts. If they have families.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: We have to be on guard...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Do you look like that... because you already knew about this?

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: You... This was part of your plan too...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It was per Military Commission of Kazdel arrangements.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Sacrifice is unavoidable, mercenary. I thought your captain would have taught you this long ago.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: You're a general! And they're your soldiers!

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Yes. I am a general, and this is my work.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Be it our enemies or ourselves, I must cast each and every life into this gaping maw we call war—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And pray it spits out the best ending we could wish for.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: That is all I can achieve in my position.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Hence why I came; I came to give this all my full attention. To look over every pale, young face here.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I must remind myself that this was a decision I made.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I will not say this is the price the Sarkaz must pay, mercenary.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The Victorians killed them, but it was I that let them be killed by the Victorians.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Why do you have to do it this way?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: To light a fire.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Light a fire that will extend across this great land.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And we... the Sarkaz, can find a place for ourselves, the room for us to exist, only on such a divided land.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Mercenary, you must learn to familiarize yourself with it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Be familiar with it. Hate it. And finally, accept it.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Because this is the only way.
A bright blaze flames high from the lockdown zone, an old building fiercely burning.

steps.name: Paprika
steps.text: Another... accident?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No. That is the first flame.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Mercenary, come with me. We must return to the airship.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Our guests have already taken their seats.
